HOSPITAL SAFETY

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Just how safe are hospital staff and patients – we go undercover at health facilities to see just how possible it is to enter with a deadly weapon.

Unique Selling Point:
Armed with hidden cameras, we expose ineffective security measures at health facility entry and exit points.

Summary:
Hospital safety often makes it into the headlines as incidents of violence on nurses and patients are frequent. Most happen on hospital and clinic premises where it it the responsibility of the health facility and department to provide adequate security. We explore some of the cases by speaking to nurses who were involved and hold authorities to account.

Further information:
As part of our research, we collected around 6 minutes of usable footage showing our team gain entry into hospitals and clinics while carrying a dangerous weapon. We also have additional footage of incidents at health facilities.

We will also share right of reply responses received in writing from the various health facilities we visited and the security companies at those facilities.

Press Release:


Safety in Public Hospitals
A knife, a pair of scissors and a few metal objects that could easily be used as weapons – in an extensive investigation covering some of Gauteng’s state-run hospitals and clinics, Carte Blanche goes inside these facilities to put their security measures to the test. With violent incidents of shootings and stabbings happening inside public health facilities, we investigate why it’s seemingly become so easy to breach hospital security.
Producers: Ntokozo Miya and Mduduzi Miya| Presenter: Masa Kekana | Research: Mosibudi Ratlebjane


Script:


HOSPITAL SAFETY – FINAL

AUDIO
VO – Nursing – a calling that attracts people who are dedicated to saving lives. But caregivers at public hospitals and clinics fear that their own lives are on the line. And the threat - the people they serve, patients.
LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION

They are going to be angry because you are taking forever to attend their emergency.
TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE

There are too many incidents with the weapons.
NEO KHAKHAU – NURSE

I wonder what will happen one day when a patient enters with a weapon, attacks me and stabs me.
LINK - Violent attacks at health facilities have left staff in panic mode, constantly wondering if the people walk into their wards have deadly intentions.
VO – Thirty-two year-old Neo Khakhau works in a ward where mothers make appointments for their babies to be immunized.
NEO KHAKHAU – NURSE

When you have missed your date, you happen to be seen last. People who are booked for the day are going to be seen first. The mom didn't want to be seen last. I just felt a slap to my face, a hot clap.
VO – There was no security guard in sight.
NEO KHAKHAU – NURSE

If it wasn't because of other patients who actually pulled the mom off me, I don't know what she would have done to me.
VO – Lerato Madumo-Gova of the Young Nurses Indaba says nurses are often in the firing line of frustrated patients at under-resourced and short-staffed facilities.
LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION

When I'm unable to deliver to your expectation, the community is mostly angry. The altercation that occurs between a patient and the nurse – it's an everyday occurrence.
VO – Patients are also at risk.
LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION

People will always say if you want to finish somebody off, it's easy to do it at a hospital.
VO – On the eleventh of January this year, two men smuggled a gun into the Clairwood Hospital in KZN and fatally shot a patient in the head.

Last year at the South Rand Hospital near Johannesburg, three men assaulted an injured man, demanding a gun he'd carried into the hospital.


UPSOUND

THUGS - The gun is here. They took the gun. We want the gun. The gun is here.
NURSES - The security guard ran away. He ran away
VO – With no one to protect them, the nurses barricaded themselves behind a locked security gate.

In most cases, guards run away because they have no weapons – guns are prohibited on hospital grounds.
LINK - Seeing as health facilities are gun-free-zones, it comes as no surprise that unarmed guards would run for cover when they come face-to-face with people carrying weapons.
VO – In December at the Levai Mbatha clinic in Evaton near Vereeniging, a mob forced its way into the facility.
LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION

One of the people that were there was stabbed. The rest of the people that he was fighting with wanted to finish him off. A few nurses had to fight, trying to save this patient.
VO – She says its easy to get a weapon inside a ward.
LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION

Vetting and ensuring that the correct people come in and go out is sometimes just completely neglected.
VO – There are no official stats to account for violent incidents, intimidation and harassment of doctors and nurses.
LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION

But the reports that we get as a union are extremely shocking. A facility such as Chiawelo will definitely have incidents that escalate way above 10 incidents, in a day.
VO – On January thirteen, two days after the Clairwood Hospital shooting, health minister Zweli Mkhize wrote that at state healthcare facilities, “it will no longer be possible to simply walk in without passing through a security checkpoint. Members of the community should expect that they may be searched.”
LINK - We went undercover to test this and see if it would actually be possible to enter a health facility armed with this knife, capable of causing serious injuries and even death.
VO – Two days after the minister's statement, we packed a braai kit including an intimidating knife and began our experiment, which would take a few days. At the Chiawelo clinic, there was no guard at the pedestrian entrance and we simply walked in with the knife. We strolled around the clinic but couldn't get inside the maternity ward. We pretended we were friends of a nurse who works there.
UPSOUND

NURSE: Please call her. ... We are scared. You don't just ask for Joyce and get Joyce. (beep over name)... There are incidents.




VO – Next to the metal detector entrance at the Charlotte Maxeke Hospital in Johannesburg, is a door without a detector. We enter through the latter and none of the four guards queries this or searches the bag containing the knife.

The metal detector beeps when we walk into the South Rand Hospital with the knife but no one pays any attention. We carry the blade inside with no hassles.

At Soweto's Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital, a look through the back window of the car and a friendly greeting are all it takes us to get past the main gate with a deadly weapon.
UPSOUND

CB: How are things?
GUARD: Very good, my brother. You?
CB: All is well.
VO – At the Helen Joseph Hospital in Joburg during visiting hours, males are scanned with a portable metal detector. Guards take a quick look inside our female operative's bag and don't notice the knife.

At all the facilities, the knife would have been discovered had a proper been conducted. We were able to get inside most service areas except maternity wards where stringent security measures apply.

A 2018 report notes that more than a billion rands was spent on security services at state healthcare facilities in the 2016/2017 financial year, which raises the question as to whether or not there is value for money.

Andre Mundell, a consultant with over thirty years experience in the security sector, says poor access control is an open invitation to criminals.
ANDRE MUNDELL – INDEPENDENT SECURITY CONSULTANT

Even when you don't have criminal intentions, if the opportunity is always there, you'll take a chance. We don't only measure incidents, we measure the opportunity that creates the incidents.
VO – Regular risk assessments are necessary to stay ahead of criminals.
ANDRE MUNDELL – INDEPENDENT SECURITY CONSULTANT

The hospitals...never have a risk assessment so the question I ask them is what homework, what research was done to establish the type of security that they have .
VO – We shared our findings with the health department's Arnold Malotana.
MASA - No one even really bothered to check our bags. What's your reaction as a department to this?

ARNOLD MALOTANA - It's a very scary thought, really cause for concern, and I think it's something that we should and we will follow up on it.
VO – It's unfortunate that some security companies don't perform according to their contracts.
ARNOLD MALOTANA – DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

You'll understand that we have 54 companies contracted to the across all 300 institutions and that the level of performance across all will not be the same.
VO – The department takes security breaches seriously and often acts decisively against negligent contractors.
ARNOLD MALOTANA – DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH
We've terminated contracts and said look: “You've failed in your obligations to protect the institution that you have been paid for, using public money.”
VO – Despite security breaches, there have been successes.
ARNOLD MALOTANA – DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

A baby was snatched from the maternity unit, where within hours, following the CCTV, producing a picture of who the suspect was, … the baby was found.
The security company at Helen Joseph Hospital said their guards are “well-trained and thorough in executing their functions... this is just an unfortunate situation and it will be rectified.”

The Bara entrance is on a main road and its contractor says due to traffic, it's “not practical and feasible” to search every car. The company says it has “upskilled the training of the personnel.”

The security service providers at the South Rand Hospital, Chiawelo Clinic and Charlotte Maxeke did not respond to our queries in time for this broadcast.
VO – Sex-fueled incidents are also common. Last year at the Pelonomi Hospital in the Free State, a doctor bit off her attacker's tongue during a rape attempt.

Sowetan nurse Tiisetso Moorosi says a patient once followed her into a room in the clinic.
TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE

I told him that whatever that you are going to be doing to me, there's a camera there. And he was like: “Ja, you're lucky, I'll get you outside.”
VO – Nurses say they often take the blame for problems they are not responsible for – such as delayed service because the ward is short-staffed.

Tiisetso was on duty in December when Themba Maseko, arrived at the clinic, anxious to get help for his son who was born in a taxi on the way to the labour ward. The nurse, Tiisetso's colleague, was delayed.
TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE

They had another emergency inside the ward. When she went out, already the escort was aggravated, escort which is the father of the baby.
UPSOUND

THEMBA MASEKO: I'm not fighting. I'm asking why she is saying she won't help us because nurses deliver babies inside the ward and not in cars.
VO – Mother and child were transferred to Bara where they were stabilised and later discharged. But the matter did not end there. Tiisetso claims Themba began stalking the nurse, and one time, brought eight people with him.



TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE

I saw Themba again at the parking lot. Later on when they were knocking off, Themba was waiting at the gate. He said he wants a one-on-one confrontation with her.
VO – The nurse eventually took out a protection order. Themba says his frustration is justified but denies being a stalker.
THEMBA MASEKO - FATHER

My baby waited outside for about 18 minutes without any help.

MASA QUESTION – If a group of men or women then approach you to say they want to talk about what happened, the mess-up, surely, you understand that maybe the nurse feels intimidated and a little bit threatened?

THEMBA MASEKO - 01:06:54:18 – Based on what has happened, and then now, here's a group of men coming to me, then I will feel intimidated.
VO – Though he understands why the nurse may have been scared, Themba says his group was not aggressive.
THEMBA MASEKO – FATHER

There were 9 of us demanding to know why this happened. I didn't say: “Hey leaders, this is what they did at Chiawelo clinic. Let's go and attack.” No,no, no.
VO – An internal investigation is under way.

The unsafe working environment is emotionally draining for nurses.
TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE

Waking up, you question yourself: “Do I really need to be here?”
NEO KHAKHAU – NURSE

01:46:19:13 – If I had a choice, I would say I will stop being a nurse but nursing is the only thing that I know. I went into nursing when I was nineteen and I have been in this profession ever since so this is the only thing that I know. And we also need to make a living, what else can we do?

PROMOS

Vicious assaults and murders at healthcare facilities have left nurses and doctors panicked, worried that their next shift might very well be their last.

Healthcare professionals and patients under attack! Following a spate of violent incidents, we investigate the adequacy of hospital security.

Just how effective are security measures at hospitals – we go undercover to see if it would possible it is to enter hospitals armed with a dangerous weapon.

Carte Blanche HD mihle@combinedartists.co.za 20 February 2020 Press Release: Safety in Public Hospitals A knife, a pair of scissors and a few metal objects that could easily be used as weapons – in an extensive investigation covering some of Gauteng’s state-run hospitals and clinics, Carte Blanche goes inside these facilities to put their security measures to the test. With violent incidents of shootings and stabbings happening inside public health facilities, we investigate why it’s seemingly become so easy to breach hospital security. Producers: Ntokozo Miya and Mduduzi Miya| Presenter: Masa Kekana | Research: Mosibudi Ratlebjane Script: HOSPITAL SAFETY – FINAL AUDIO VO – Nursing – a calling that attracts people who are dedicated to saving lives. But caregivers at public hospitals and clinics fear that their own lives are on the line. And the threat - the people they serve, patients. LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION They are going to be angry because you are taking forever to attend their emergency. TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE There are too many incidents with the weapons. NEO KHAKHAU – NURSE I wonder what will happen one day when a patient enters with a weapon, attacks me and stabs me. LINK - Violent attacks at health facilities have left staff in panic mode, constantly wondering if the people walk into their wards have deadly intentions. VO – Thirty-two year-old Neo Khakhau works in a ward where mothers make appointments for their babies to be immunized. NEO KHAKHAU – NURSE When you have missed your date, you happen to be seen last. People who are booked for the day are going to be seen first. The mom didn't want to be seen last. I just felt a slap to my face, a hot clap. VO – There was no security guard in sight. NEO KHAKHAU – NURSE If it wasn't because of other patients who actually pulled the mom off me, I don't know what she would have done to me. VO – Lerato Madumo-Gova of the Young Nurses Indaba says nurses are often in the firing line of frustrated patients at under-resourced and short-staffed facilities. LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION When I'm unable to deliver to your expectation, the community is mostly angry. The altercation that occurs between a patient and the nurse – it's an everyday occurrence. VO – Patients are also at risk. LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION People will always say if you want to finish somebody off, it's easy to do it at a hospital. VO – On the eleventh of January this year, two men smuggled a gun into the Clairwood Hospital in KZN and fatally shot a patient in the head. Last year at the South Rand Hospital near Johannesburg, three men assaulted an injured man, demanding a gun he'd carried into the hospital. UPSOUND THUGS - The gun is here. They took the gun. We want the gun. The gun is here. NURSES - The security guard ran away. He ran away VO – With no one to protect them, the nurses barricaded themselves behind a locked security gate. In most cases, guards run away because they have no weapons – guns are prohibited on hospital grounds. LINK - Seeing as health facilities are gun-free-zones, it comes as no surprise that unarmed guards would run for cover when they come face-to-face with people carrying weapons. VO – In December at the Levai Mbatha clinic in Evaton near Vereeniging, a mob forced its way into the facility. LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION One of the people that were there was stabbed. The rest of the people that he was fighting with wanted to finish him off. A few nurses had to fight, trying to save this patient. VO – She says its easy to get a weapon inside a ward. LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION Vetting and ensuring that the correct people come in and go out is sometimes just completely neglected. VO – There are no official stats to account for violent incidents, intimidation and harassment of doctors and nurses. LERATO MADUMO-GOVA – YOUNG NURSES INDABA TRADE UNION But the reports that we get as a union are extremely shocking. A facility such as Chiawelo will definitely have incidents that escalate way above 10 incidents, in a day. VO – On January thirteen, two days after the Clairwood Hospital shooting, health minister Zweli Mkhize wrote that at state healthcare facilities, “it will no longer be possible to simply walk in without passing through a security checkpoint. Members of the community should expect that they may be searched.” LINK - We went undercover to test this and see if it would actually be possible to enter a health facility armed with this knife, capable of causing serious injuries and even death. VO – Two days after the minister's statement, we packed a braai kit including an intimidating knife and began our experiment, which would take a few days. At the Chiawelo clinic, there was no guard at the pedestrian entrance and we simply walked in with the knife. We strolled around the clinic but couldn't get inside the maternity ward. We pretended we were friends of a nurse who works there. UPSOUND NURSE: Please call her. ... We are scared. You don't just ask for Joyce and get Joyce. (beep over name)... There are incidents. VO – Next to the metal detector entrance at the Charlotte Maxeke Hospital in Johannesburg, is a door without a detector. We enter through the latter and none of the four guards queries this or searches the bag containing the knife. The metal detector beeps when we walk into the South Rand Hospital with the knife but no one pays any attention. We carry the blade inside with no hassles. At Soweto's Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital, a look through the back window of the car and a friendly greeting are all it takes us to get past the main gate with a deadly weapon. UPSOUND CB: How are things? GUARD: Very good, my brother. You? CB: All is well. VO – At the Helen Joseph Hospital in Joburg during visiting hours, males are scanned with a portable metal detector. Guards take a quick look inside our female operative's bag and don't notice the knife. At all the facilities, the knife would have been discovered had a proper been conducted. We were able to get inside most service areas except maternity wards where stringent security measures apply. A 2018 report notes that more than a billion rands was spent on security services at state healthcare facilities in the 2016/2017 financial year, which raises the question as to whether or not there is value for money. Andre Mundell, a consultant with over thirty years experience in the security sector, says poor access control is an open invitation to criminals. ANDRE MUNDELL – INDEPENDENT SECURITY CONSULTANT Even when you don't have criminal intentions, if the opportunity is always there, you'll take a chance. We don't only measure incidents, we measure the opportunity that creates the incidents. VO – Regular risk assessments are necessary to stay ahead of criminals. ANDRE MUNDELL – INDEPENDENT SECURITY CONSULTANT The hospitals...never have a risk assessment so the question I ask them is what homework, what research was done to establish the type of security that they have . VO – We shared our findings with the health department's Arnold Malotana. MASA - No one even really bothered to check our bags. What's your reaction as a department to this? ARNOLD MALOTANA - It's a very scary thought, really cause for concern, and I think it's something that we should and we will follow up on it. VO – It's unfortunate that some security companies don't perform according to their contracts. ARNOLD MALOTANA – DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH You'll understand that we have 54 companies contracted to the across all 300 institutions and that the level of performance across all will not be the same. VO – The department takes security breaches seriously and often acts decisively against negligent contractors. ARNOLD MALOTANA – DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH We've terminated contracts and said look: “You've failed in your obligations to protect the institution that you have been paid for, using public money.” VO – Despite security breaches, there have been successes. ARNOLD MALOTANA – DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH A baby was snatched from the maternity unit, where within hours, following the CCTV, producing a picture of who the suspect was, … the baby was found. The security company at Helen Joseph Hospital said their guards are “well-trained and thorough in executing their functions... this is just an unfortunate situation and it will be rectified.” The Bara entrance is on a main road and its contractor says due to traffic, it's “not practical and feasible” to search every car. The company says it has “upskilled the training of the personnel.” The security service providers at the South Rand Hospital, Chiawelo Clinic and Charlotte Maxeke did not respond to our queries in time for this broadcast. VO – Sex-fueled incidents are also common. Last year at the Pelonomi Hospital in the Free State, a doctor bit off her attacker's tongue during a rape attempt. Sowetan nurse Tiisetso Moorosi says a patient once followed her into a room in the clinic. TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE I told him that whatever that you are going to be doing to me, there's a camera there. And he was like: “Ja, you're lucky, I'll get you outside.” VO – Nurses say they often take the blame for problems they are not responsible for – such as delayed service because the ward is short-staffed. Tiisetso was on duty in December when Themba Maseko, arrived at the clinic, anxious to get help for his son who was born in a taxi on the way to the labour ward. The nurse, Tiisetso's colleague, was delayed. TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE They had another emergency inside the ward. When she went out, already the escort was aggravated, escort which is the father of the baby. UPSOUND THEMBA MASEKO: I'm not fighting. I'm asking why she is saying she won't help us because nurses deliver babies inside the ward and not in cars. VO – Mother and child were transferred to Bara where they were stabilised and later discharged. But the matter did not end there. Tiisetso claims Themba began stalking the nurse, and one time, brought eight people with him. TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE I saw Themba again at the parking lot. Later on when they were knocking off, Themba was waiting at the gate. He said he wants a one-on-one confrontation with her. VO – The nurse eventually took out a protection order. Themba says his frustration is justified but denies being a stalker. THEMBA MASEKO - FATHER My baby waited outside for about 18 minutes without any help. MASA QUESTION – If a group of men or women then approach you to say they want to talk about what happened, the mess-up, surely, you understand that maybe the nurse feels intimidated and a little bit threatened? THEMBA MASEKO - 01:06:54:18 – Based on what has happened, and then now, here's a group of men coming to me, then I will feel intimidated. VO – Though he understands why the nurse may have been scared, Themba says his group was not aggressive. THEMBA MASEKO – FATHER There were 9 of us demanding to know why this happened. I didn't say: “Hey leaders, this is what they did at Chiawelo clinic. Let's go and attack.” No,no, no. VO – An internal investigation is under way. The unsafe working environment is emotionally draining for nurses. TIISETSO MOOROSI – NURSE Waking up, you question yourself: “Do I really need to be here?” NEO KHAKHAU – NURSE 01:46:19:13 – If I had a choice, I would say I will stop being a nurse but nursing is the only thing that I know. I went into nursing when I was nineteen and I have been in this profession ever since so this is the only thing that I know. And we also need to make a living, what else can we do? PROMOS Vicious assaults and murders at healthcare facilities have left nurses and doctors panicked, worried that their next shift might very well be their last. Healthcare professionals and patients under attack! Following a spate of violent incidents, we investigate the adequacy of hospital security. Just how effective are security measures at hospitals – we go undercover to see if it would possible it is to enter hospitals armed with a dangerous weapon.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Just how safe are hospital staff and patients – we go undercover at health facilities to see just how possible it is to enter with a deadly weapon.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Armed with hidden cameras, we expose ineffective security measures at health facility entry and exit points.
metadata.Summary: Hospital safety often makes it into the headlines as incidents of violence on nurses and patients are frequent. Most happen on hospital and clinic premises where it it the responsibility of the health facility and department to provide adequate security. We explore some of the cases by speaking to nurses who were involved and hold authorities to account.
metadata.Further information: As part of our research, we collected around 6 minutes of usable footage showing our team gain entry into hospitals and clinics while carrying a dangerous weapon. We also have additional footage of incidents at health facilities. We will also share right of reply responses received in writing from the various health facilities we visited and the security companies at those facilities.
